bites.title: One painting, seven layers
bites.body: Here's a production pipeline from the bottom of the stack to the top: Flats (solid silhouettes) Local color (clipped to flats) Shadow (Multiply) Contact shadow (Multiply, darker, tight) Rim light (Add or Screen) Paintover (normal, on top) Plus a Rough sketch floating above everything at low opacity while you work.

bites.title: Rough
bites.body: New layer named Rough. Sketch something simple and loose: an apple on a table, a head, a robot.

bites.title: Flats
bites.body: New layer below Rough named Flats. Fill the silhouette with one solid mid color. The fill tool ({key:KritaFill/KisToolFill|F}) helps.

bites.title: Local color
bites.body: Above Flats: Local, with Inherit Alpha on (or Ctrl+Shift+G from lesson 09). Paint the object's real colors; they can't escape the silhouette.

bites.title: Shadow
bites.body: Above Local: Shadow, blend mode Multiply, clipped. Paint the shadow shapes in one cool gray or purple. Multiply darkens everything under it naturally.

bites.title: Contact shadow
bites.body: Above Shadow: Contact, Multiply again. Small, dark, tight: where things touch, the table under the apple, the crease of a sleeve.

bites.title: Rim light
bites.body: Above Contact: Rim, blend Addition or Screen. A thin bright edge on the side away from the light. Instant drama.

bites.title: Paintover
bites.body: On top: Paintover, normal mode, no clipping. Fix edges, add highlights, unify. Turn the Rough down below 50% or hide it.

bites.title: 17 cleared
bites.body: Every part of the painting is on its own layer, with its own blend mode, all editable. Art directors love you already.
